functions.note: RadiansToDegrees(Acos(From | To)) in double; Acos clamps its argument to [-1, 1]. The inputs are expected to be unit vectors (not normalized by the function), result in [0, 180].

Python type: unreal.Vector3f (float32 components). Both vectors are projected to XY and FVector2f::Normalize() is applied: if |v|^2 <= UE_SMALL_NUMBER (1e-8) the 2D vector is SET TO ZERO (so a zero / tiny vector gives dot 0 and cross 0, result 0); result = RadiansToDegrees(Acos(FromXY | ToXY)) * FMath::Sign(FromXY ^ ToXY). FMath::Sign(0) is 0, so exactly parallel AND exactly opposite vectors return 0 (antiparallel gives 0, not +-180).

functions.signature: FVector SlerpSkipNormalization(const FVector& From, const FVector& To, float Ratio)
functions.note: Dot > 0.9995 -> GetSafeNormal(Lerp(From, To, Ratio)); else Theta = Acos(max(-1, Dot)) * Ratio (float), result = From * cos(Theta) + Normalize(To - From * Dot) * sin(Theta). Inputs are expected to be unit vectors. For (nearly) opposite vectors the perpendicular is zero/degenerate.

functions.signature: FVector SpringDamperVector(FAlsSpringVectorState& SpringState, const FVector& Current, const FVector& Target, float DeltaTime, float Frequency, float DampingRatio, float TargetVelocityAmount = 1.0f)
functions.note: The Python call does NOT mutate the passed state struct; it returns (value, new_state). state_in / state_out are the FAlsSpring*State fields (Velocity, PreviousTarget, bStateValid). C++: DeltaTime <= UE_SMALL_NUMBER returns Current and leaves the state untouched; an invalid state returns Target, zeroes Velocity, stores PreviousTarget=Target and sets bStateValid; otherwise FMath::SpringDamper is run with TargetVelocity = (Target - PreviousTarget) * Clamp01(TargetVelocityAmount) / DeltaTime. The state vectors are FVector (double).
